guia.what: A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen without fully covering what’s behind it. For secondary or long content—filters, a cart, navigation, details—where keeping the context matters. It uses the same `<dialog>` engine as the Modal.
whenUse: The content is long, or it helps to keep a sense of where it came from.
Filters, navigation, a cart, or a side detail that opens and closes often.
On small screens, where an edge-to-edge panel works better than a centered box.
whenAvoid: The task is brief and deserves the screen’s full attention → `modal`.
It’s only a menu of actions anchored to a trigger → `menu` or `popover`.
dos: Choose the side deliberately (`side-left`, `side-right`…)—navigation at the start, details and filters at the end (RTL-aware).
Give it a header with a title and an explicit close button, in addition to Esc.
donts: Don’t put the page’s main task in a drawer. If it’s the core work, it belongs on the page.
Don’t use it for a passing notice—that’s a `toast` or a `banner`.

teclado.action: Closes the panel. If it isn’t dismissible (`closedby="none"`), it does nothing, not even on a second Esc in a row.

nucleo: It’s a `<dialog>` with invoker commands (`commandfor`), with CSS transforms to slide in from the side.
